newsitem.title: EGYPT: Moslem cleric says force last option for Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Moslem cleric says force last option for Jerusalem.

text.p: One of the Sunni Moslem world's highest religious authorities said on Thursday that if peace talks with Israel failed, Jerusalem must be taken by force and anyone who died fighting for it would be a martyr.
Sheikh Mohammed Sayyed Tantawi, the head of Al-Azhar, the most respected Islamic learning institution, was speaking at an international conference on Jerusalem.

"All of us are determined to restore our rights...but through legal ways, such as negotiations and dialogue. If they prove to be futile...and if Israel proceeds on the way of its aggression and injustice and continues swallowing Palestinian lands, we must defend Jerusalem.
"If we do not get our rights back by negotiations, we must get them by force," said Tantawi. "Death for the sake of seeking our legitimate rights is a sort of holy war and martyrdom."
Tantawi, considered a liberal among Egyptian Moslem clerics, sponsored the conference called "Jerusalem: Focus of Peace" at Al Azhar University.

Peace talks between Israel and the Palestinians collapsed in March when Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu gave the go-ahead for construction of 6,500 homes for Jews in East Jerusalem. An attack followed on a Tel Aviv cafe the same month and a Palestinian bomber and three Israeli women were killed.
Some Moslems consider suicide bombings against Israeli targets as legitimate and see killed bombers as martyrs.
Officials for Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat held talks on Wednesday aimed at exploring the chances of resuming formal peace negotiations.

Israel annexed East Jerusalem and declared all of the city its eternal and indivisible capital after the 1967 Middle East war. The PLO wants East Jerusalem as the capital of a future Palestinian state.
